Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Vincent Kompany Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at Bayern training
 Bayern Munich head coach had been nursing a virus
 Coach ‘undergoing thorough examinations’, club say
 Reuters Fri 23 Oct 2026 12.50 EDT Last modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 17.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Vincent Kompany has been ⁠taken ⁠to ​hospital after the Bayern Munich coach felt unwell during training ⁠on Friday.
 The Belgian, ​who ‌had been ‌nursing a virus in ‌recent days, was coaching his team before feeling unwell and being taken to ‌hospital.
 The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 ​at home against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, are due ​to ​travel to ​Freiburg on Sunday. Kompany was on the bench for the Arsenal game despite the viral infection.
 Bayern said on their website: “Vincent Kompany required medical ⁠attention after collapsing during a training session for ​Bayern’s reserve team. The ‌head coach of the professional squad had been observing ‌the second team’s session.
 “Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training ‌and match-related operations.“
 Max Eberl, Bayern’s sporting director, said: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. At Bayern, we will do everything ​we ​can to ensure he ​makes a speedy recovery.
 “Vinnie is receiving ​all the ‌necessary medical care ​and ​support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”
